title: Pre-Analysis (Closed) — Doubler Family Extension to the Aft Belly Fairing Panels
abstract: Closed pre-analysis of a proposal to extend the pre-qualified doubler family aft of the belly fairing, rejected because the panel thickness and the frame pitch change and the existing substantiation does not carry across.

sections.objective: Establish whether the four pre-qualified doubler sizes could be extended to the panels immediately aft of the belly fairing, where operators reported the same class of ground handling damage.
sections.findings_summary: Three items were confirmed and the proposal was rejected. The substantiation behind the family assumes a panel thickness band and a frame pitch that both change aft of the fairing, so the same doubler in the same size carries a different load path there and the fastener pattern edge distances no longer hold. The repair scheme itself was found to be clear about this, but the investigation task's selection chart could easily be read as applying to any lower shell panel, which is a documentation risk that existed before this proposal and was raised separately. The bulletin that released the family states the panel population explicitly and would have needed re-issue rather than amendment. Extending the family would have required a fresh substantiation campaign that nobody was prepared to fund for a damage rate roughly a fifth of the forward area.
sections.next_steps: Proposal rejected. A documentation change was raised to make the selection chart's panel population explicit, and the aft area was left on the repair approval route.

similarity_seeds: a repair standard applied outside the population it was substantiated for

expected_findings.rationale: The edge distance and fastener pattern in the repair scheme are substantiated for the forward panel thickness band. Aft of the fairing the thickness and the frame pitch both change and the same doubler carries a different load path.
expected_findings.resolution: Reject the extension; the aft area stays on the repair approval route.

expected_findings.rationale: The investigation task's selection chart does not state the panel population explicitly and could be read as covering any lower shell panel, which is a risk independent of this proposal.
expected_findings.resolution: Raise a documentation change to state the panel population in the chart.

expected_findings.rationale: The releasing bulletin names the panel population, so any extension needs a re-issue rather than an amendment.
expected_findings.resolution: No action; recorded for the next attempt.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned because it is another metallic repair with blend limits and doubler straps in similar language, but it covers floor panel supports inside the cabin, with a different load path and no shared identifier with the proposal.

type_data.conclusion: Closed. Extension rejected on substantiation grounds; a chart wording change was raised separately.
